questions.question: Two trains, running between Bangalore and Chennai, start at the same time from their respective locations and proceed towards each other at the speed of 80 km/h and 95km/h. When they meet, it is found that one train has travelled 180 km more than the other. The distance between Bangalore and Chennai is ______
questions.questionHtml: Two trains, running between Bangalore and Chennai, start at the same time from their respective locations and proceed towards each other at the speed of 80 km/h and 95km/h. When they meet, it is found that one train has travelled 180 km more than the other. The distance between Bangalore and Chennai is ______
questions.solution:
Let the time of traveling be 't' hours

Distance traveled by train with speed 80 km/h = (80 × t), and distance traveled by train with speed 95 km/h = (95 × t) 

According to the question, The difference in distance traveled by two trains = 180 km 

⇒ 95 t - 80t = 180 ⇒ 15t =  180 ⇒ t = 12 hours 

Distance between stations = 80 ×12 + 95 × 12  = 960 + 1140 = 2100km

questions.question: One third part of a certain journey is covered at the speed of 10 km/hr, one fourth part at the speed of 15 km/hr and the rest part at the speed of 20 km/hr. What will be the average speed for the whole journey?
questions.questionHtml: One third part of a certain journey is covered at the speed of 10 km/hr, one fourth part at the speed of 15 km/hr and the rest part at the speed of 20 km/hr. What will be the average speed for the whole journey?
questions.solution:
T1 = (x/3)/S1 = x/30 hr, T2 = (x/4)/S2 = x/60 hr

Remaining Distance = x - (x/3) - (x/4) = 5x/12

T3 = (5x/12)/S3 = x/48 hr

Total time = T1 + T2 + T3 = (x/30) + (x/60) + (x/48) = 17x/240

Average Speed = Total Distance/Total Time = x/(17x/240) = 240/17 km/hr

questions.question: How much time (in minutes) will a dog take to run around a square field of side 75 m if it runs at the rate of 6 km/hr?
questions.questionHtml: How much time (in minutes) will a dog take to run around a square field of side 75 m if it runs at the rate of 6 km/hr?
questions.solution:
Given:

Square of side = 75 m

And a dog runs around the square with a speed of = 6 km/hr

Formula Used:

The perimeter of a square = 4 × side of the given square

Calculation:

⇒ Speed of the dog in m/sec = 6 × 1000/3600 = 6× 5/18 = 5/3 m/sec

⇒ The perimeter of the Square = 4 × 75 m = 300 m

⇒ Time = Distance/speed

Hence, Time is taken by the dog to travel around the square

⇒ Time = (300)/(5/3) = 60 × 3 seconds or (60 × 3)/60 = 3 minutes

questions.question: The speeds of two bodies are in the ratio 2 : 3. If the difference in the time taken to cover 50 m is 10 sec, then find the difference in their speeds.
questions.questionHtml: The speeds of two bodies are in the ratio 2 : 3. If the difference in the time taken to cover 50 m is 10 sec, then find the difference in their speeds.
questions.solution:
We know, when distance is constant, then speed ∝ 1/time

The speeds of two bodies are in the ratio 2 : 3, then, time ratio of two bodies 3 : 2

Difference in the time (3 - 2) = 1 unit → 10 sec, then 3 unit → 10 × 3 = 30 sec and 2 unit  → 10 × 2 = 20 sec

So, body 1 takes time to cover 50 m is 30 sec, Speed = 50/30 = 5/3m/s

And body 2 takes time to cover 50 m is 20 sec, Speed = 50/20 = 5/2 m/s

Speed difference = (5/2 - 5/3) = 5/6 m/s

questions.question: In a linear race of 1000 m, Prakash beats Ved by 280 m, while Ved beats Rahul by 100 m. By how many metres does Prakash beat Rahul, in the same race?
questions.questionHtml: In a linear race of 1000 m, Prakash beats Ved by 280 m, while Ved beats Rahul by 100 m. By how many metres does Prakash beat Rahul, in the same race?
questions.solution:
Prakash : Ved = 1000 : (1000 - 280) = 1000 : 720 = 25 : 18    

Ved : Rahul = 1000 : (1000 - 100) = 1000 : 900 = 10 : 9           

A : B = 125 : 90

B : C = 90 : 81

Now, Prakash : Ved : Rahul = 125 : 90 : 81

Prakash covers 1000 then Rahul covers = 81 × 8 = 648

Prakash will beat Rahul in a race of 1000 m = 1000 - 648 = 352 m

questions.question: A man covers a certain distance by bike. If he covers 25% of the distance at the speed of 25 km/h, 50% of the distance at the speed of 50 km/h and the remaining distance at the speed of 12.5 km/h, find his average speed over the whole journey.
questions.questionHtml: A man covers a certain distance by bike. If he covers 25% of the distance at the speed of 25 km/h, 50% of the distance at the speed of 50 km/h and the remaining distance at the speed of 12.5 km/h, find his average speed over the whole journey.
questions.solution:
Let total distance = D km

Distance covered at Speed1 ⇒ 0.25D, Time1 ⇒ (0.25D) / 25

Distance covered at Speed2 ⇒ 0.5D, Time2 ⇒ (0.5D) / 50

Distance covered at Speed3 ⇒ 0.25D, Time3 ⇒ (0.25D) / 12.5

Total time ⇒ (0.25D/25) + (0.5D/50) + (0.25D/12.5)

Total time ⇒ D/100 + D/100 + D/50 ⇒ (D/100) + (D/100) + (2D/100) ⇒ 4D/100 ⇒ D/25

Average speed ⇒ D / (D/25) ⇒ 25 km/h

questions.question: A train covers a certain distance in 45 minutes. If its speed is reduced by 5 km/h, it takes 5 minutes more to cover the same distance. The distance (in km) is:
questions.questionHtml: A train covers a certain distance in 45 minutes. If its speed is reduced by 5 km/h, it takes 5 minutes more to cover the same distance. The distance (in km) is:
questions.solution:
Given:

Time taken to cover a certain distance = 45 min

If speed reduced by 5 km/h then it takes 5 minutes more

Formula used:

Distance = Speed × Time

Calculation:

Let the distance be ‘D’ and speed be ‘s’

According to the question,

⇒ D/s = 45/60

⇒ D/s = 3/4

⇒ s = 4D/3

If speed reduced by 5 km/h, time becomes (45 + 5)minutes

⇒ D/(s – 5) = 50/60

⇒ 6D = 5s – 25

⇒ 6D = 5(4D/3) – 25

⇒ 20D/3 – 6D = 25

⇒ 2D/3 = 25

⇒ D = 37.5 km

∴ The distance (in km) is 37.5 km

questions.question: Kivand and Dinesh travel a distance of 60 km such that the speed of Kivand is faster than Dinesh. The sum of their speeds is 80 km/h and the total time taken by both is 3 hours 12 minutes. Find the speed of Kivand?
questions.questionHtml: Kivand and Dinesh travel a distance of 60 km such that the speed of Kivand is faster than Dinesh. The sum of their speeds is 80 km/h and the total time taken by both is 3 hours 12 minutes. Find the speed of Kivand?
questions.solution:
Given:

Distance travelled = 60 km

Kivand faster than Dinesh

Sum of speeds of Kivand and Dinesh = 80 km/hr

Total time taken by both = 3 hours 12 min

Concept used:

Speed = distance /time

Calculation:

Let the speed of Kivand be K km/hr and Dinesh be D km/hr

Then ,sum of speeds = K + D = 80 km/hr       ----(1)

Total time = 60/K + 60/D = 3 + (12/60) hours

60/K + 60/D = 16/5      ----(2)

Let us use options along with (1) and (2) to arrive at the solution.

option 1 not possible as it is said that Kivand is faster than Dinesh.

Option 2 not possible as when K = 30 km/hr then D = 80 - 30 = 50 km/hr. Here also, K not greater than D

Option 3, K = 50 km/hr then, D = 80 - 50 = 30 km/hr

Applying these values in (2), the equation becomes, 60/50 + 60/30 = 6/5 + 2 = 16/5 hours

∴ We can conclude that speed of Kivand is 50 km/hr.

questions.question: Anuj and Anup have to travel from a place A to a place B in their respective cars. Anuj is driving at 70 km/h, and takes 3 halts of 10 minutes each, while Anup is driving at 80 km/h, and takes 4 halts of 15 minutes each. The time taken by Anup to reach Place B, if Anuj takes 8.5 hours, is:
questions.questionHtml: Anuj and Anup have to travel from a place A to a place B in their respective cars. Anuj is driving at 70 km/h, and takes 3 halts of 10 minutes each, while Anup is driving at 80 km/h, and takes 4 halts of 15 minutes each. The time taken by Anup to reach Place B, if Anuj takes 8.5 hours, is:
questions.solution:
Total halt time of Anuj = 3 × 10 = 30 minutes = 0.5 hours

Actual driving time of Anuj = 8.5 - 0.5 = 8 hours

Total distance = 8 × 70 = 560 km.

Total halt time of Anup = 4 × 15 = 60minutes = 1 hours 

The time taken by Anup to reach Place B = 560 / 80  = 7 hours

Total time = 7 + 1 = 8 hours.

questions.question: Ravi starts for his school from his house on his cycle at 8:20 a.m. If he runs his cycle at a speed of 10 km/h, he reaches his school 8 minutes late, and if he drives the cycle at a speed of 16 km/h, he reaches his school 10 minutes early. The school starts at:
questions.questionHtml: Ravi starts for his school from his house on his cycle at 8:20 a.m. If he runs his cycle at a speed of 10 km/h, he reaches his school 8 minutes late, and if he drives the cycle at a speed of 16 km/h, he reaches his school 10 minutes early. The school starts at:
questions.solution:
GIven:

Ravi starts from his house to school at 8:20 a.m with speed of 10 km/h and reaches 8 minutess late

If he ride the cycle at speed of 16 km/h he reaches his school 10 minutes early

Formula used:

Calculation:

Let the distance between home and school be x km

And time take to reach school at the time be t hrs

With the speed of 10 km/h, Ravi reaches 8 minutes late

⇒ x/10 = t + 8/60

⇒ x/10 = t + 2/15      ----(1)

With the speed of 16 km/h, Ravi reaches 10 minutes early

⇒ x/16 = t – 10/60

⇒ x/16 = t – 1/6      ----(2)

Now, Subtract (2) from (1)

⇒ x/10 – x/16 = t + 2/15 – t + 1/6

⇒ (5x – 8x)/80 = (4 + 5)/30

⇒ 3x × 30 = 9 × 80

⇒ x = 720/90

⇒ x = 8 km

Now, put the value of x in (1)

⇒ 8/10 = t + 2/15

⇒ t = 8/10 – 2/15

⇒ t = (24 – 4)/30 

⇒ t = 2/3

To convert it into minutes by 60

⇒ (2/3) × 60 = 40 minutes

College starts at 8:20 + 40 mins = 9 A.M

∴ College starts at 9 A.M

 

⇒ 8x = 48 minutes

Ravi is 8 min late, the correct time will be

⇒ 48 - 8 = 40 minutes

College starts at 8:20 + 40 mins = 9 A.M

∴ College starts at 9 A.M

questions.question: If a train 130 m long takes 6 \(\frac{1}{2}\) seconds to cross a man who is walking at 12 km/h in the same direction in which the train going, then the speed of the train (in km/h) is:
questions.questionHtml: If a train 130 m long takes 6\(\frac{1}{2}\) seconds to cross a man who is walking at 12 km/h in the same direction in which the train going, then the speed of the train (in km/h) is:
questions.solution:

So Relative speed  will be 130/6.5 = 20 m/s

 Relative speed  is 20 × 18/5 = 72 km/h

The speed of the train will be  72 +12 = 84 km/h

questions.question: A car travels with a speed of 21 m/sec in the first 10 minutes, 9.0 km in the next 10 minutes and 10 km in the last 10 minutes of its journey. What is the average speed of the car in km/h during its entire journey?
questions.questionHtml: A car travels with a speed of 21 m/sec in the first 10 minutes, 9.0 km in the next 10 minutes and 10 km in the last 10 minutes of its journey. What is the average speed of the car in km/h during its entire journey?
questions.solution:
In the first 10 minutes car travels with a speed of 21m/s             [1 min = 60 sec then 10 min = 600 sec]

Distance travelled = 21 × 600 = 12600 m = 12.6 km then Total distance travelled = 12.6 + 9 + 10 = 31.6 km 

Total time taken = (10 + 10 + 10) minutes = 30 min = 30/60 = 1/2 h 

Average speed = 31.6/(1/2) = 31.6 ×  2 = 63.2 km/h

questions.question: In an 800 m race, the ratio of the speeds of two contestants Ankur and Neha is 5 ∶ 6. If Ankur has a head-start of 200 m, then Ankur will win by _____.
questions.questionHtml: In an 800 m race, the ratio of the speeds of two contestants Ankur and Neha is 5 ∶ 6. If Ankur has a head-start of 200 m, then Ankur will win by _____.
questions.solution:
Let speed of Ankur = 5 units, speed of Neha = 6 units

Head-start for Ankur = 200 m, remaining distance = 600 m

Time taken by Ankur = 600/5 = 120 units

Distance covered by Neha in 120 units = 120 × 6 = 720 m

Neha loses by 800 - 720 = 80 m

questions.question: Train 'A' runs at a speed of 80 kmph and leaves station 'X' at 11 a.m. Train 'B' leaves station 'X' at 11.15 a.m. in the same direction. On the same day. At what speed train 'B' should run in order to catch train 'A' at station 'Y' located at a distance of 60 km?
questions.questionHtml: Train 'A' runs at a speed of 80 kmph and leaves station 'X' at 11 a.m. Train 'B' leaves station 'X' at 11.15 a.m. in the same direction. On the same day. At what speed train 'B' should run in order to catch train 'A' at station 'Y' located at a distance of 60 km?
questions.solution:
Given,

Train 'A' runs at a speed of 80 kmph and leaves station 'X' at 11 a.m. Train 'B' leaves station 'X' at 11.15 a.m. in the same direction. On the same day.

Station 'Y' located at a distance of 60 km.

The train 'A' will reach the station 'Y' at,

Time = \(Distance / Speed\)

Time = 60/80 = 3/4 hr = 45 min.

∴ The train 'A' will reach the station 'Y' at 11:45 a.m.

∴ To catch train 'A' at the station 'Y', the train 'B' must reach at 11:45 a.m. to the station 'Y'.

So, the train 'B' leaves the station 'X' at 11:15 a.m. and to catch the train 'A', the train 'B' must travel 60 km in 30 min (1/2 hr).

∴ Speed = \(Distance / Time \)

∴ Speed = 60 ÷ 1/2 = 60 × 2 = 120 kmph

Hence, the correct answer is 120 km/h.

questions.question: In a race of 1200 m, Ram can beat Shyam by 200 m or by 20 sec . What must be the speed of Ram?
questions.questionHtml: In a race of 1200 m, Ram can beat Shyam by 200 m or by 20 sec. What must be the speed of Ram?
questions.solution:
GIVEN:

In a race of 1200 m 

Ram can beat shyam by 200 m or by 20 sec

FORMULA USED:

Distance = Speed × Time 

CALCULATION:

Here, Ram beats shyam by 200 m or 20 sec

This means shyam covers 200m distance in 20 sec

Speed of shyam = 200/20 = 10m/s 

Also, in 1200m race ram beats shyam by 200m

This also means distance covered by ram = 1200m 

Distance covered by shyam = 1000m 

So, 1000 m  distance is covered by shyam = 10m/s 

Then, 1200 m distance will be covered by ram  = 10/1000 × 1200 = 12m/s 

Hence, speed of  the ram is 12m/s .

questions.question: A train crosses two persons travelling at 4 km/h and 6 km/h in the same direction in 12 sec and 14 sec, respectively. The speed of the train is ______.
questions.questionHtml: A train crosses two persons travelling at 4 km/h and 6 km/h in the same direction in 12 sec and 14 sec, respectively. The speed of the train is ______.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For a train crossing two objects in the same direction:

Speed of Train (V) = (S2 × T2 − S1 × T1) ÷ (T2 − T1)

V = (6 × 14 − 4 × 12) ÷ (14 − 12)

V = (84 − 48) ÷ 2 = 36 ÷ 2 = 18 km/h

∴ The correct answer is 18 km/h.

Alternate Method

Given:

Speed of person 1 (v1) = 4 km/h | Time (t1) = 12 s

Speed of person 2 (v2) = 6 km/h | Time (t2) = 14 s

Let the speed of the train be V km/h and the length of the train be L meters.

Formula Used:

Distance = Relative Speed × Time

Length of train (L) is constant in both cases.

⇒ L = (V − 4) × (5/18) × 12 — (i)

⇒ L = (V − 6) × (5/18) × 14 — (ii)

Equating (i) and (ii):

⇒ (V − 4) × 12 = (V − 6) × 14

⇒ 12V − 48 = 14V − 84

⇒ 14V − 12V = 84 − 48

⇒ 2V = 36

⇒ V = 18 km/h

∴ The correct answer is 18 km/h.

Additional Information

Relative Speed Concepts

When two objects move in the same direction, relative speed = V1 − V2. When they move in opposite directions, relative speed = V1 + V2.

Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Train Crossing a Point Object

When a train crosses a pole, person, or tree, the distance covered is exactly equal to the length of the train.

questions.question: Zeenat and Nasreen participate in a circular race of 1.2 km. They start the race at a speed of 18 km/h and 27 km/h. respectively, from the same point at the same time. After how much time (in minutes) will they meet at the starting point for the first time, if they are running in the same direction?
questions.questionHtml: Zeenat and Nasreen participate in a circular race of 1.2 km. They start the race at a speed of 18 km/h and 27 km/h. respectively, from the same point at the same time. After how much time (in minutes) will they meet at the starting point for the first time, if they are running in the same direction?
questions.solution:
Relative speed will be (27 - 18) km/h = 9 km/h

The relative distance is 1.2 km .

So the time will be, ⇒ (1.2 / 9) × 60 ⇒ 0.4 × 20 = 8 minutes.

questions.question: Vivek starts moving at the speed of 70 km/hr at 8 ∶ 00 am. Neeraj starts moving in the same direction after 4 hours of Vivek at the speed of 120 km/hr. Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct? I. Neeraj and Vivek meet each other at 5 ∶ 36 pm. II. Total distance covered by both Neeraj and Vivek till 4 pm is 1080 km.
questions.questionHtml:
Vivek starts moving at the speed of 70 km/hr at 8 ∶ 00 am. Neeraj starts moving in the same direction after 4 hours of Vivek at the speed of 120 km/hr. Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?

I. Neeraj and Vivek meet each other at 5 ∶ 36 pm.

II. Total distance covered by both Neeraj and Vivek till 4 pm is 1080 km.
questions.solution:
Vivek covers from 8:00 am to 12:00 pm (4 hours): = 70 km/hr × 4 hr = 280 km

Time by Neeraj to catch up with Vivek: Relative speed of Neeraj with respect to Vivek = 120 km/hr - 70 km/hr = 50 km/hr

Time taken by Neeraj to catch up with Vivek = Distance between them / Relative speed = 280 km/50 km/hr = 5.6 hours

Since Neeraj started 4 hours after Vivek, the time on the clock when they meet would be: Time = 8:00 am + 4 hr + 5.6 hr = 05 : 36 pm. Statement I is correct.

Total distance covered by both Neeraj and Vivek till 4 pm:

Distance covered by Vivek = 70 km/hr × 8 hr = 560 km

Distance covered by Neeraj = 120 km/hr × 4 hr = 480 km

Total distance covered by both = 560 km + 480 km = 1040 km. Statement I is correct.

questions.question: A person takes 40 minutes more than his usual time when he covers a distance of 20 km at 5 km/h. If he covers the same distance at 10 km/h, he takes x minutes less than the usual time. What is the value of x ?
questions.questionHtml: A person takes 40 minutes more than his usual time when he covers a distance of 20 km at 5 km/h. If he covers the same distance at 10 km/h, he takes x minutes less than the usual time. What is the value of x ?
questions.solution:
Given:

Speed of man = 5 km/h

Distance = 20 km

Formula used:

Time = Distance/Speed

Calculation:

According to the question,

In first condition:

Time = Distance/Speed = 20/5 = 4 hr

Usual time = 4 hr – 40 min = 3 hr and 20 min

In Second condition:

Speed of man = 10 km/hr

Time = Distance /Speed = 20/10 = 2 hr 

Time difference = (3 hr + 20 min) – (2 hr ) = 1 hr 20min = (60 + 20)min = 80 min

∴ The required answer will be 80 min.

 Alternate Method

Calculation:

Time = \(\frac{{{\rm{Distance}}}}{{{\rm{Speed}}}}\)

T1 = \(\frac{{20}}{5} = 4km/hr\)

T2 = \(\frac{{20}}{{10}} = 2km/hr\)

T1 : T2 = 2 : 1

Usual time = T1 and new time = T2

As per the question,

Difference of time = 40 unit

⇒ 2 unit - 1 unit = 40 unit

⇒ 1 unit = 40 unit

Usual time = 2 unit = 2 × 40 

Usual time = 80 

∴ The required answer will be 80 min.

Shortcut Trick \(\frac{{{\rm{S1\times S2}}}}{{{\rm{ S2- S1}}}} \times \frac{{{\rm{T1 +T2}}}}{{{\rm{60}}}} = 20\)

Where,

S1 = Speed of man

S2 = Speed of man

S1 < S2

T1 = Extra time

T2 = Usual time 

\(\frac{{{\rm{10 \times 5}}}}{{{\rm{10 - 5}}}} \times \frac{{{\rm{40 +x}}}}{{{\rm{60}}}} = 20\)

⇒ \(\frac{{{\rm{50}}}}{{{\rm{5}}}} \times \frac{{{\rm{40 +x}}}}{{{\rm{60}}}} = 20\)

⇒ 40 + x = 120

⇒ x = 120 - 40 = 80 min.

questions.question: Aman decided to cover a distance of 12 km in 78 minutes. He decided to cover the initial two - thirds of the distance at 10 km/h and the remaining at some different speed. Find the speed for the last one - third of the distance.
questions.questionHtml: Aman decided to cover a distance of 12 km in 78 minutes. He decided to cover the initial two - thirds of the distance at 10 km/h and the remaining at some different speed. Find the speed for the last one - third of the distance.
questions.solution:
Time taken to cover 1st 12 × 2/3 = 8 km distance ⇒ 8 × 60/10 = 48 minutes

Remaining time 78 - 48 = 30

Remaining distance 12 - 8 = 4 km

He has to travel 4 km in 30 minutes 

So the speed will be 4 × 2 = 8 km/h

questions.question: A takes 3 hours more than B to walk 'd' km. If A doubles his speed, then he can make it in 1 hour less than B. How much time (in hours) does A require to walk 'd' km?
questions.questionHtml: A takes 3 hours more than B to walk 'd' km. If A doubles his speed, then he can make it in 1 hour less than B. How much time (in hours) does A require to walk 'd' km?
questions.solution:

(d/a) - (d/b) = 3      ----(i), (d/b) - (d/2a) = 1      ----(i)

By adding eq (i) and eq (ii) we get,

d/2a = 4 ⇒ d/a = 4 × 2 = 8

questions.question: In a 1500 m race, Anil beats Bakul by 150 m and in the same race Bakul beats Charles by 75 m. By what distance does Anil beat Charles?
questions.questionHtml: In a 1500 m race, Anil beats Bakul by 150 m and in the same race Bakul beats Charles by 75 m. By what distance does Anil beat Charles?
questions.solution:
When Anil completes the race, Bakul covered (1500 - 150) = 1350 m

In a 1500 m race Charles is 75 m behind Bakul

So, in 1350 m race Charles is 75/1500 × 1350 = 67.5 m behind Bakul

So, Charles is (67.5 + 150) = 217.5 m behind from Anil in 1500 m race

Anil beat Charlie by 217.50 m.

questions.question: In a journey of three unequal laps, a car covers a distance of 200 km in 4 h in the first lap, while another 162 km at the speed of 15 m/s in the second lap. It covered the remaining distance of the final lap in 4 h such that the average speed of the car for entire journey was 50 km/h. What was the speed of the car in the third lap of the journey?
questions.questionHtml: In a journey of three unequal laps, a car covers a distance of 200 km in 4 h in the first lap, while another 162 km at the speed of 15 m/s in the second lap. It covered the remaining distance of the final lap in 4 h such that the average speed of the car for entire journey was 50 km/h. What was the speed of the car in the third lap of the journey?
questions.solution:
Given:

A car covers a distance of 200 km in 4 h in the first lap

162 km at the speed of 15 m/s in the second lap

It covered the remaining distance of the final lap in 4 h

Concept Used:

Average speed = Total Distance traveled/Total time taken

Calculation:

Distance covered in first lap = 200 km, Time taken = 4 h

Distance covered in second lap = 162 km, speed = 15 m/s

= 15 × \(\frac{18}{5}\) = 54 km/h

Time taken = \(\frac{162}{54}\) = 3h

Let the distance covered in the 3rd lap = x km

Time taken = 4h

Average Speed = \(\frac{200 \ + 162 \ + \ x}{4 +\ 3 + \ 4}\)

⇒ \(\frac{200 \ + 162 \ + \ x}{4 +\ 3 + \ 4}\) = 50km/h

⇒ 362 + x = 50 × 11

⇒ x = 550 - 362 = 188 km

So, the speed in 3rd lap = 188/4 = 47km/h

Therefore, the speed of the car in the third lap of the journey is 47 km/h

questions.question: In 1 km linear race, P beats Q by 120 metres or 30 sec. What is the time taken by P to cover the race?
questions.questionHtml: In 1 km linear race, P beats Q by 120 metres or 30 sec. What is the time taken by P to cover the race?
questions.solution:
"P" beats "Q" by 120 m or 30 sec,

Speed of "Q" = 120/30 = 4 m/s

Time to cover 1000 m = 1000/4 = 250 sec

"P" beats "Q" by 30 sec means "P" reach 30 sec early

Time taken by "A" to complete the race = 250 – 30 = 220 sec

questions.question: In a 400-metre race, A runs at a speed of 16 m/sec. If A gives B a start of 15 metres and still beats him by 10 sec, then what is the speed of B?
questions.questionHtml: In a 400-metre race, A runs at a speed of 16 m/sec. If A gives B a start of 15 metres and still beats him by 10 sec, then what is the speed of B?
questions.solution:
Time taken by A = 400/16 = 25 seconds

B has to cover = 400 - 15 = 385 metres

Time taken by B = 25 + 10 = 35 seconds

Speed of B = 385/35 = 11 m/s

questions.question: If a person travels at a speed of 48 km/h, he will reach his destination on time. He covers two-thirds of his journey in five-sixths of time. At what speed (in km/h) should he travel to cover the remaining distance to reach his destination on time?
questions.questionHtml: If a person travels at a speed of 48 km/h, he will reach his destination on time. He covers two-thirds of his journey in five-sixths of time. At what speed (in km/h) should he travel to cover the remaining distance to reach his destination on time?
questions.solution:
Given:

Normal speed of the person = 48 km/h

Concept used:

Speed = Distance/Time

Calculation:

Let he usually travels for 6x hours

So. his total distance = 48 × 6x

⇒ 288x km

According to the question,

He covered 288x × 2/3 = 192x km in 5x hours

So remaining 288x - 192x = 96x km

He will cover it in x hours

So, speed = 96x/x = 96 km/h

∴ He should travel 96 km/h to cover the remaining distance to reach his destination on time.

questions.question: Rahul and Mithun travel a distance of 30 km. The sum of their speeds is 70 km/h and the total time taken by both to travel the distance is 2 hours 6 minutes. The difference between their speeds is:
questions.questionHtml: Rahul and Mithun travel a distance of 30 km. The sum of their speeds is 70 km/h and the total time taken by both to travel the distance is 2 hours 6 minutes. The difference between their speeds is:
questions.solution:
Given 

 Rahul and Mithun travel  = 30 km 

Sum of their speed = 70 km/h

Formula used 

Distance = speed × time 

Calculation 

let the speed of rahul = s 

⇒ speed of mithun = 70 - s 

⇒ total time = 2(6/60) hr = 21/10 hr 

⇒ 30/s + {30/(70 - s)} = 21/10 

⇒ s2 - 70s + 1000 = 0

⇒ s2 - 50s - 20s + 1000 = 0 

⇒ s(s - 50) - 20(s - 50) = 0 

⇒ (s - 50) (s - 20) = 0 

⇒ s = 50 km/hr , s = 20 km/hr 

when speed of Rahul = 50 km/hr , speed of mithun = 20 km/hr 

when speed of mithun = 50 km/hr , speed of rahul = 20 km.hr 

∴ The difference of their speed is 30 km/hr

questions.question: The distance between two places is 1200 km. To cover this distance, a person X takes 5 hours lesser than another person Y, whose average speed is 40 km/h lesser than that of X. The time taken by Y to complete the travel is:
questions.questionHtml: The distance between two places is 1200 km. To cover this distance, a person X takes 5 hours lesser than another person Y, whose average speed is 40 km/h lesser than that of X. The time taken by Y to complete the travel is:
questions.solution:
1200/(S - 40) - 1200/S = 5 ⇒ (S)2 - (40 × S) - 9600 = 0 ⇒ (S - 120) (S + 80) = 0 ⇒ S = 120 km/h

Speed of Y = (120 - 40) = 80 km/h

Time taken by Y = 1200/80 = 15 hours

questions.question: X and Y start at the same time to ride from place A to place B, which is 80 km away from A. X travels 4 km per hour slower than Y. Y reaches place B and at once turns back, meeting X, 16 km from place B. Y's speed (in km/h) is:
questions.questionHtml: X and Y start at the same time to ride from place A to place B, which is 80 km away from A. X travels 4 km per hour slower than Y. Y reaches place B and at once turns back, meeting X, 16 km from place B. Y's speed (in km/h) is:
questions.solution:
Given:

X and Y start at the same time to ride from place A to place B, which is 80 km away from A

X travels 4 km per hour slower than Y

Y reaches place B and at once turns back meeting X, 16 km from place B.

Calculation:

Let the speed of X be p km/hr

The speed of Y = (p + 4) km/hr

Distance travelled by Y = (80 + 16) = 96 km/hr

Distance travelled by X = (80 – 16) = 64 km/hr

According to the question

⇒ 96/(p + 4) = 64/p

⇒ 96p = 64p + 256

⇒ 32p = 256

⇒ p = 8 km

Now,

The speed of Y is (p + 4) = (8 + 4)

⇒ 12 km/hr

∴ The required speed of Y is 12

questions.question: The wheel of a car has 210 cm diameter. How many revolutions per minute must the wheel make so that the speed of the car is kept at 120 km/h?
questions.questionHtml: The wheel of a car has 210 cm diameter. How many revolutions per minute must the wheel make so that the speed of the car is kept at 120 km/h?
questions.solution:
Given:

Diameter if wheel,D = 210 cm = 2.1 m

Speed of car, v = 120 km/hour

Formula used:

V = (πDN)/60

V → speed, D → diameter, N → number of revolution

Calculatioon:

V = (πDN)/60

⇒ 120 × 5/18 = (π × 2.1 × N)/60

1 km/hour = 5/18 m/s

⇒ N = (120 × 5 × 60)/(18 × 2.1 × π)

⇒ N = 303.03

∴ Revolution of wheel in a minute is 303.03

questions.questionHtml: Farhan and Aman are going from Delhi to Haryana. The difference and sum of their speeds are 40 km/hour and 60 km/hour respectively. If in a race Farhan can finish 8 minutes earlier than Aman, then find the distance they both should cover.

questions.question: In a linear race of 1000 m, A beats B by 50 m or 5 seconds. What is the difference between the speeds (in m/s) of A and B?
questions.questionHtml: In a linear race of 1000 m, A beats B by 50 m or 5 seconds. What is the difference between the speeds (in m/s) of A and B?

questions.question: A car travels for 11 hours. For the first 100 km, the car travels with a certain speed, and then it increases its speed by 15 km/h to cover the remaining 280 km. The time (in hours) it takes to travel the 100 km part is:
questions.questionHtml: A car travels for 11 hours. For the first 100 km, the car travels with a certain speed, and then it increases its speed by 15 km/h to cover the remaining 280 km. The time (in hours) it takes to travel the 100 km part is:
questions.solution:
Given:

Car travel for 11 hours.

First 100 km, he traveled at a certain speed,

Remaining 280km distance traveled by the increased speed by 15km/hr

Formula Used:

Speed = Distance/Time

ax2 + bx + c = 0,

To solve the quadratic equation for bigger numbers,

Use for x = {b +/- √(b2  – 4ac)}/2a

Calculation:

Time = Distance/Speed

A car traveled for 11 hours.

Let the initial speed of a car be x

⇒ 11 = 100/x + 280/(x + 15)

⇒ 11 = {100(x + 15) + 280x}/x(x + 15)

⇒ 11 = {100x + 1500 + 280x}/x2 + 15x

⇒ 11(x2 + 15x) = 380x + 1500 

⇒ 11x2 + 165x = 380x + 1500

⇒ 11x2 + 165x – 380x – 1500 = 0

⇒ 11x2 – 215x – 1500 = 0

Compairing with the quadratic equation ax2 + bx + c = 0,

we get,

a = 11, b = – 215, c = –1500

Using formula {–b +/- √(b2  – 4ac)}/2a

⇒ {–(– 215) +/- √(– 2152  – 4(11)(–1500))}/2(11)

⇒ {215 +/- √(46225 + 66,000)}/22

⇒ {215 +/- √1,12,225}/22

⇒ (215 +/- 335)/22

⇒ (215 + 335)/22 OR (215 – 335)/22

⇒ 550/22 OR –120/22

⇒ 25 OR –5.4545

Speed can not be negative

Initial speed of a car is 25km/hr.

Speed = Distance/Time

⇒ 25 = 100/Time

⇒ Time = 100/25

⇒ Time = 4 hours.

∴ Time taken by him to cover 100km distance is 4 hours.

questions.questionHtml: In a 140 m race, Pankaj runs at a speed of \(\frac{5}{2}\)m/s. He gives a start of 20 m to Arun and still defeats him by 4 seconds. The speed of Arun is:

questions.question: A car and a bus were both travelling in the same direction. At 7.30 a.m., the car, moving at 72 km/h, was 4.2 kilometres behind the bus. The car was 15.8 kilometres ahead of the bus at 8:15 a.m. What is the ratio of the speed of the car to that of the bus?
questions.questionHtml: A car and a bus were both travelling in the same direction. At 7.30 a.m., the car, moving at 72 km/h, was 4.2 kilometres behind the bus. The car was 15.8 kilometres ahead of the bus at 8:15 a.m. What is the ratio of the speed of the car to that of the bus?
questions.solution:
Calculation:

Speed of car = 72 km/h

Distance covered by car in 1 hour i.e. 60 minutes = 72 km

Distance covered by car in 45 minutes (from 7 : 30 a.m to 8 : 15 a.m) = 54 km [i.e. (72/60) × 45]

Distance covered by bus in 45 minutes = (54 - 4.2 - 15.8) km = 34 km

When time is constant then,

The speed of the car ∶ The Speed of the Bus = Distance covered by car ∶ Distance covered by bus in 45 minutes = 54 ∶ 34

27 ∶ 17

questions.question: A car covers 20 km in the first quarter of an hour, 25 km in the second quarter of that hour and 15 km in the third quarter. The average speed of the car (in km/h) over the entire journey is:
questions.questionHtml: A car covers 20 km in the first quarter of an hour, 25 km in the second quarter of that hour and 15 km in the third quarter. The average speed of the car (in km/h) over the entire journey is:
questions.solution:
Total distance = 20 km + 25 km + 15 km = 60 km,

Total time = 3/4 hours

Average speed = 60 km / (3/4) = 60 × (4/3) = 80 km/h

questions.question: In a 120 metre race, P beats S by 6 metres. If S starts with a head start of 7.5 metres and it is a 100 metre race, then who wins the race and how many metres? (Correct to 2 decimal places)
questions.questionHtml: In a 120 metre race, P beats S by 6 metres. If S starts with a head start of 7.5 metres and it is a 100 metre race, then who wins the race and how many metres? (Correct to 2 decimal places)
questions.solution:
Given :

In a race of 120 m, P beats S by 6m

In the race of 100 m, S has a head start of 7.5 m

Formula Used :

Speed = Distance / Time

Calculation :

Let the speed of P and Q be a and b respectively.

If P beats S by 6 m, it means in the same time P runs 120 m while Q runs 114 m.

Then, 120 / a = 114 / b

⇒ a / b = 120 / 114 = 60 / 57        --------(1)

Now in the race of 100 m, S starts with a head start of 7.5 m which means S runs 92.5 m.

Let in same time P runs y m.

Then, y / a = 92.5 / b

⇒ y = \(\frac{a}{b} \times 92.5\)

⇒ y = \(\frac{60}{57} \times 92.5\) = 97.37

Thus, P will run only 97.37 m.

Therefore P loses the race by (100 - 97.37) m = 2.63 m

∴ S wins the race by 2.63 m.

questions.question: A and B run a 12 km race on a circular track of length 1200 m. They complete one round in 300 seconds and 400 seconds, respectively. After how much time from start will the faster person meet the slower person for the last time?
questions.questionHtml: A and B run a 12 km race on a circular track of length 1200 m. They complete one round in 300 seconds and 400 seconds, respectively. After how much time from start will the faster person meet the slower person for the last time?
questions.solution:
Given:

A and B run a 12 km race 

Length of circular track = 1200 m

Time taken by A to complete the first round = 300 seconds

Time taken by B to complete the first round = 400 seconds

Formula Used:

Distance = Speed × Time 

Calculation:

Here,

We have 12 km i.e. 12000 m race in a circular track of the length of 1200 m.

Number of round to complete the race = 12000/1200 = 10 rounds

Now,

Time taken by A to complete the first round = 300 seconds

For 10 rounds it will take 300 × 10 = 3000 seconds 

Now,

When A and B both start running,

First meet will take place in L.C.M (300,400) seconds = 1200 sec

Next meet will take place =  1200 × 2 = 2400 seconds

For next meet,

Time would  be 3600 seconds, which is Not possible as A completes the race in 3000 seconds

But, to complete 10 rounds A takes 3000 seconds. So, time cannot be more than 3000 seconds

So, faster person will meet the slower person last time at 2400 seconds

Hence, A will meet B last time at 2400 seconds.

questions.question: A takes 2 hours 30 minutes more than B to walk 40 km. If A doubles his speed, then he can make it in 1 hour less than B. How much time (in hours) does A require for walking a 40 km distance?
questions.questionHtml: A takes 2 hours 30 minutes more than B to walk 40 km. If A doubles his speed, then he can make it in 1 hour less than B. How much time (in hours) does A require for walking a 40 km distance?

Time = Distance/ Speed

Time taken by A to cover the distance 40/x hour

Time taken by B (40/x - 2.5) hours

When A doubles his speed time taken by A 40/2x hour

Accordingly,

 [(40/x) – 2.5)] – (40/2x) = 1

⇒ (40/x) – (40/2x) = 3.5

⇒ 40/2x = 7/2

⇒ x = 40/7

Time taken by A to cover the distance 40 ÷ (40/7) 

⇒ 7 hours

questions.question: In a race of 400 m, Bhim gave Saral a head start by 20 m at the start of the race. Saral took 48 seconds to complete the race. What was the speed (in m/s) of Bhim if Saral defeated Bhim by a margin of 2 seconds?
questions.questionHtml: In a race of 400 m, Bhim gave Saral a head start by 20 m at the start of the race. Saral took 48 seconds to complete the race. What was the speed (in m/s) of Bhim if Saral defeated Bhim by a margin of 2 seconds?
questions.solution:
Given:

Distance of the race = 400 m

Time taken by Saral to complete the race = 48 seconds

Margin by which Saral defeated Bhim = 2 seconds

Formula Used:

Speed = Distance / Time

Calculation:

Time taken by Bhim to complete the race (as Bhim loses the race) = Time taken by Saral + Margin

⇒ Time taken by Bhim to complete the race = 48 + 2

⇒ Time taken by Bhim to complete the race = 50 seconds

As, Distance covered by Bhim = 400 m

Speed of Bhim = 400/50 = 8 sec

Hence, the Speed of Bhim is 8 m/s.

questions.question: The distance between the places H and O is D units. The average speed that gets a person from H to O in a stipulated time is S units. He takes 20 minutes more time than usual if he travels at 60 km/h, and reaches 44 minutes early if he travels at 75 km/h. The sum of the numerical values of D and S is:
questions.questionHtml: The distance between the places H and O is D units. The average speed that gets a person from H to O in a stipulated time is S units. He takes 20 minutes more time than usual if he travels at 60 km/h, and reaches 44 minutes early if he travels at 75 km/h. The sum of the numerical values of D and S is:
questions.solution:
Given:

Distance between H and O = D km

Average speed = S km/hr

The average speed that gets a person from H to O in a stipulated time is S units. He takes 20 minutes more time than usual if he travels at 60 km/h, and reaches 44 minutes early if he travels at 75 km/h. 

Formula:

Speed = Distance/time

Average speed = Total distance/Total time

Calculation:

Let right time for the train to cover its journey (in minutes) be t hrs, then

As we know,

Distance = Speed × Time

According to the question

60 × (t + 20/60) =  75 × (t - 44/60)

⇒ 4 (t + 1/3) = 5 (t - 11/15)

⇒ 4t + 4/3 = 5t - 11/3

⇒ 5t – 4t = 11/3 + 4/3

⇒ t = 11/3 + 4/3

⇒ t = 5 hrs

Distance (D) = 60 × (5 + 20/60)

⇒ D = 60 × (5 + 1/3)

⇒ D = 60 × (16/3)

⇒ D = 320  km

Distance between H and O is 320 km.

Average speed (S) = 320/5 = 64 km/hr

∴ Sum of numerical values of D and S = 320 + 64 = 384

questions.question: In a 1500 m race, if vehicle P gives vehicle Q a start of 200 m, then vehicle P wins the race by 8 sec. Alternatively, if vehicle P gives vehicle Q a start of 400 m, the race ends in a dead heat. How long does vehicle P take to run 1500 m?
questions.questionHtml: In a 1500 m race, if vehicle P gives vehicle Q a start of 200 m, then vehicle P wins the race by 8 sec. Alternatively, if vehicle P gives vehicle Q a start of 400 m, the race ends in a dead heat. How long does vehicle P take to run 1500 m?
questions.solution:
Vehicle P gives vehicle Q a start of 200 m, and P wins the race by 8 sec, which means P travels 1500 m and Q travels 1300 m

Speed of P = \(\frac{1500}{t}\) and speed of Q = \(\frac{1300}{t+8}\)   [Let the time taken by P is t]

Now, if vehicle P gives vehicle Q a start of 400 m, race is draw, which means P travels 1500 m and Q travels 1100 m

\(\frac{1500}{\frac{1500}{t}}=\frac{1100}{\frac{1300}{t+8}}\) ⇒  \(t=\frac{11(t+8)}{13}\) ⇒ 2t = 88 ⇒ t = 44 sec

questions.question: A thief steals an item and escapes, running at 13.5 km/h. A policeman arrives at the spot of the crime after 8 minutes and immediately starts chasing the thief. 28 minutes after the policeman started to chase the thief, there is still a gap of 540 m between the two. At what distance from the spot of the crime would the policeman catch up with the thief, and what is the speed (in km/h) at which the policeman ran?
questions.questionHtml: A thief steals an item and escapes, running at 13.5 km/h. A policeman arrives at the spot of the crime after 8 minutes and immediately starts chasing the thief. 28 minutes after the policeman started to chase the thief, there is still a gap of 540 m between the two. At what distance from the spot of the crime would the policeman catch up with the thief, and what is the speed (in km/h) at which the policeman ran?
questions.solution:
Given: Speed of thief = 13.5 km/h

Distance covered by thief in 8 min = 13.5 × (8/60) = 1.8 km

Distance covered by thief in 28 min = 13.5 × (28/60) = 6.3 km

Total distance covered by thief = 1.8 + 6.3 = 8.1 km

Gap = 8.1 - 0.54 = 7.56 km,

Speed of policeman = (7.56 × 60)/28 = 16.2 km/h,

Time to cover gap = (540 × 18)/(2.7 × 5) = 720 s,

Distance covered by thief in 720 s = (13.5 × 720)/3600 = 2.7 km,

Total distance = 8.1 + 2.7 = 10.8 km.

questions.question: The force (in pound-force) needed to keep a car from skidding on a curve varies directly with the weight of the car (in pounds) and the square of its speed (in miles per hour [mph]) and inversely with the radius (in feet) of the curve. questions.questionHtml: The force (in pound-force) needed to keep a car from skidding on a curve varies directly with the weight of the car (in pounds) and the square of its speed (in miles per hour [mph]) and inversely with the radius (in feet) of the curve. Suppose 6125 pound force is required to keep a 2750 pound car, travelling at a speed of 35 mph, from skidding on a curve of radius 550 feet. Force = weight × speed2 × 1/radius × k

Force = 3600 × 502 × 1/750 × 1 = 12000

questions.question: Two places B1 and B2 are 500 km apart from each other. Sonit and Robin start moving from B1 towards B2 at the same time. After reaching B2, they return back to B1. Speed of Sonit is 80 km/hr more than the Robin. If they meet after 6 hours, then which of the following statement(s) is/are correct? I. Distance covered by Sonit is 600 km. II. Speed of Robin is 120/3 km/hr.
questions.questionHtml:
Two places B1 and B2 are 500 km apart from each other. Sonit and Robin start moving from B1 towards B2 at the same time. After reaching B2, they return back to B1. Speed of Sonit is 80 km/hr more than the Robin. If they meet after 6 hours, then which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?

I. Distance covered by Sonit is 600 km.

II. Speed of Robin is 120/3 km/hr.
questions.solution:
Let the speed of Robin is x km/hr. Distance travelled by Ronit in 6 hrs y km. Speed of Sonit = (x + 80) km/hr

The distance travelled by Sonit in 6 hrs = 500 + 500 - y = (1000 - y) km

Distance travelled by Ronit in 6hrs = 6x km = y km  

Distance travelled by Sonit in 6hrs = 6(x + 80) km

(1000 - y) = 6(x + 80) ⇒ 1000 - 6x = 6x + 480 ⇒ 12x = 520 ⇒ x = 130/3 km

Distance travelled by Sonit = 1000 - 6x ⇒ 740 km. Statement I is wrong.

Speed of Robin = 130/(3 × 6) = 130/18 km/hr  Statement II is wrong.

∴ Option 3 is the correct answer.
